items.what: Two hand-written Lua JSON encoders in one file: quote/encode in LUA_TABLE_SERIALIZER (tools/screenshots.py:41-85) and Json in LUA_SCENE (729-761); either could be the one home, with the first the more careful
items.why: Same job, drifted details. Array test: the first requires every key to be a positive integer and the count to equal #value, the second only compares #value with the key count. Maps: the first emits {"__map__":[[k,v],...]} so numeric keys survive (parse_lua_tables restores them), the second stringifies keys. Strings: the first escapes bytes below 32, quote and backslash; the second escapes %c (which also takes 127), quote and backslash, all as \u00XX. Both print inf and nan through tostring, which is not JSON. The map shape differs on purpose (Data tables are keyed by number, the scene's output by name); the rest is accidental, and a fix to one string or array rule would not reach the other.
items.reason: tools/screenshots.py holds two hand-written Lua JSON encoders (quote/encode in LUA_TABLE_SERIALIZER, Json in LUA_SCENE) for the same Python reader. A scratch run with one shared encoder rendered identical scenes. Share one encoder string between the two Lua programs? It changes how the scene's JSON is decoded (through the restore step parse_lua_tables uses), so it is a design choice rather than a mechanical edit.

items.what: decoder()'s node filter carries a dead half: "parse_lua_tables" in names and ast.FunctionDef in the first isinstance can never match
items.why: The first clause tests `getattr(node, "targets", [])`, which only an ast.Assign has, so a FunctionDef always yields an empty any() and the `"parse_lua_tables"` member of names is never compared against anything; the function is picked up solely by the second clause (`isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef) and node.name == "parse_lua_tables"`). Local to one test helper, no other reader. Fix: test `isinstance(node, ast.Assign)` against the single name LUA_TABLE_SERIALIZER and keep the FunctionDef clause, or reuse port() for the function.
items.guard: lens-only: a filter clause that can never match needs a reader; vulture sees the names as used
